judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare table of load maxima with an asterisk whose footnote appears only in the following subparagraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The asterisk's meaning is supplied by Schedule C's footnote ('If these schedules are exceeded then Schedule A will apply'), so this provision is incomplete standing alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The footnote 'If these schedules are exceeded then Schedule A will apply' is cryptic — exceeding a maximum should be prohibited, not switch schedules.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A's own note says tailmen will be employed on all runs it covers, so falling back to Schedule A when a maximum is exceeded produces an odd result.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recovery runs are expressly defined and the 100-load cap with a tailman alternative is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A excludes recovery runs from its tailman requirement, which this subparagraph complements; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practice with respect to running time' is undated and undefined, and running time is a core pay-affecting variable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D(ix) fixes a mileage-based run-time rule for The Times, and 5-L directs the parties to negotiate travel-time compensation, so running time is handled three different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single numeric maximum stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-C.2 caps News trucks at 240 loads at 148 or more pages, so two general load caps coexist for the same fleet.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practice will be continued' states no ascertainable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph A fixes a number for non-pallet trucks, so the pallet case is left entirely to extrinsic practice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '8 general floormen to be used when and where needed as directed' and the heading '(Day side, double out only)' are both imprecise, and loaders 'may be rotated' subject to a fixed staffing floor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Agreement ¶¶1 and 3 set floor manning for the Times plants and 21-D.VI addresses day-side headcount at Newspoint, so manning is fixed in several overlapping places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lunch and break periods are precise, but 'if the requirements of the operation necessitate it' is an open trigger for working through them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-N gives inside employees a paid lunch in a fixed window with a half-hour premium if worked, which the 45-minute scheduled lunch here does not track exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In line with current policy' for designated points is undefined, and 'commercial work printed but not inserted at Newspoint' is a narrow but oddly framed category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly disapplies the 'extra crew' requirement of 3-L, and the territorial reference depends on Section 1's approximate boundary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It guarantees 58 named men continued day-side employment and then says this 'is not to be interpreted as a guaranty of 58 day jobs' — the sentence undercuts itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-D.1 preserves the right to lay off and rearrange, and 5-J allows shift changes on notice, so the scope of this qualified guarantee has to be worked out against them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short posting requirement referring to Section 4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B prescribes the posting period and filling order, so the cross-reference is well anchored.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Supersedes and replaces all other agreements, memoranda or practices which would otherwise relate or be applicable' is a sweeping override closing with 'except as otherwise stated herein'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Continuation of Side Agreements memorandum says every memorandum and side agreement is continued and deemed updated, and 21-C.3(g) expressly defers to the Newspoint Agreement — a direct clash of priority rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to an undefined 'IBM stipulation', promises locker review 'in a fair and equitable manner', and bundles four unrelated commitments under 'it is understood'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-C.3(e) already provides that home delivery runs will not service non-franchise dealers, so the franchise-exclusivity promise is duplicated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The actuarial mechanism is stated precisely, but it fixes funding cost 'for the calendar year 1966' in a 1981-84 agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-I.1 establishes a joint Pension Fund with percentage contributions, so a separate News company plan funded by actuarial determination sits alongside it without any stated relationship.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line direction to select an option; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The options in (a) and (b) are alternatives, and 21-F.1 makes the funding depend on which is chosen; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The anti-offset and no-change-without-approval commitments are stated definitely, though keyed to 1970 and 1964 dates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-F contains a parallel Times anti-offset provision and 22-G.1 an insurance analogue, all consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Benefits shall be provided under a new pension plan, the terms of which shall be jointly agreed upon' is an agreement to agree with no fallback.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-F.1's actuarial arbitration covers funding cost but not plan terms, so a deadlock on terms has no mechanism; 13-I.1 provides the joint Fund alternative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Improvements which, taken in their entirety, are more favorable' is a comparative judgment the words do not tell you how to make, and the whole clause is conditioned on mutual agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Pension/Welfare parity letter contains a similar most-favoured-union promise with different carve-outs, so two overlapping parity commitments exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is acknowledgment language ('the parties acknowledged', 'the parties also recognize') that creates no obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It functions as a recital for the operative 21-G.2, and its stated recognition of the need for efficiency points the opposite way from 21-G.2's absolute veto.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such concept shall not be put into effect without agreement of the NMDU' is an absolute veto stated in one line after an agreement to negotiate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-B and 3-D.1 give the Publisher unilateral rights over routes and deliveries, and 16-M.3's consent requirement is subject to a hearing remedy this clause lacks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subject and the start date are supplied only by bracketed editorial insertions, so the sentence is incomplete as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 19 already fixes the term to March 30, 1984, making this separate expiry either redundant or slightly different.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commit themselves to the achievement of maximum productivity and efficiency ... consistent with the terms of this memorandum and of the contract' is aspirational, and the following sentence immediately qualifies it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is recital-style language whose productivity commitment points against the detailed manning guarantees in Supplementary Agreement ¶¶1 and 3 and the jurisdiction grants that follow.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extracted text is badly interleaved, so the sentence about storage areas runs into an unrelated Sta-Hi sentence and the Wednesday colour-section duty is barely legible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-H.1 preserves other unions' prevailing mailroom jurisdiction, which is exactly what these exclusive Carlstadt grants displace.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise physical definition of where an insert tying line begins and ends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The identical definition is given for press tying lines, and the Control Room clause allocates console functions by reference to both; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or percentage equivalent of the city circulation which is approximately 4' is unreadable as a fraction or percentage, so the quantum of jurisdiction is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel PTL clause uses the same 'percentage equivalent of city circulation' formula without a figure, so neither supplies the missing number.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Four-sheets' is an undefined trade term but the grant is otherwise absolute and short.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the combo-run and city-completes grants around it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'City completes' is an undefined trade term; the grant itself is unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-C.a refers to Sunday completes kicking off 'as heretofore', which is the only other use; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise physical definition mirroring the ITL definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used by the City delivery and Control Room clauses; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or percentage equivalent of city circulation' is an alternative measure with no percentage given, leaving the extent of jurisdiction open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The combo-run ITL clause uses the same open formula, so the two together leave the delivery department's share unquantified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extract is a fragment beginning 'truck loaders, including, but not limited to' with the subject and verb missing, so no complete proposition appears.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing words are found in the Offloading paragraph where they were interleaved, meaning the grant only makes sense read with that clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The jurisdictional boundary is fixed by physical reference points and is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the ITL/PTL boundary definitions using the same wire machine landmark.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short and absolute allocation of stacking, storing and handling of tied bundles.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-A.1 already covers tiers and floor men, and 2-H.1 preserves other unions' mailroom jurisdiction, which this exclusivity may displace.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or any other operation under the jurisdiction of the delivery department' is a general catch-all appended to a list of named operations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The General Statement adds a second catch-all based on 43d Street practice, so two open-ended jurisdiction clauses stack on the same list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Odds' is an undefined trade term, though 'for West Side direct delivery' bounds it geographically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-C.3(c) assigns making up the odds to home delivery routemen at The News, using the same undefined term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any operations over which the delivery department had jurisdiction at 43d Street, whether by contract or by precedent' is the paradigm general catch-all following an enumerated list, and 'by precedent' imports unwritten practice wholesale.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-H.1 freezes other unions' prevailing mailroom jurisdiction and 2-B extends coverage to work performed exclusively by unit employees, so three overlapping jurisdiction rules apply at Carlstadt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Under any and all operating conditions a minimum of one' is precise, and the exclusion of ITL/PTL operators is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Agreement ¶1 adds a utility man on each Carlstadt shift and ¶3 sets a combined floor-hire minimum of 81, so several manning floors coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The break options are printed as 'two 165-minute coffee breaks or one 80-minute coffee break', figures that cannot be right and that do not correspond to each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-N provides a paid lunch within a defined window for inside employees with a premium if worked, which this 40-minute scheme does not track.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '80 minutes for lunch' for truck loaders is anomalous against the 40 minutes for floormen, and 'as the office may direct, to full capacity or to partial capacity' is an aside that does not change the entitlement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-C.d sets exactly the same relief periods (20 minutes per trailer, 15 per suburban and mail bag truck) as a separate Times commitment, an unexplained duplication.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The commitments are precise but keyed to 60 days from ratification and to a March 31, 1977 deadline, and the extract reads 'a location 150 miles from Columbus Circle' without 'at least' or 'no more than'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D Point Two (iii) requires transfer points 'more than 150 miles' from Columbus Circle for long runs, so the unqualified '150 miles' here is ambiguous against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence stops mid-clause at 'is at a location further', so the condition governing alternative destinations is missing entirely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D Point Two (iv) still lists Hightstown, New Jersey as a transfer point in use, while this clause eliminates it — a direct inconsistency within the same memorandum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise commitment tied to a named company, a named destination and a 60-day period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-E requires Board approval for changes in methods and extent of delivery, which this direct-delivery conversion effects unilaterally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends a phrase by page reference in a superseded 1973-75 booklet, so the provision cannot be applied without a document outside this instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D Point Two (ix) as printed here already states the 27-mile rule, making this amendment redundant or, if the booklet differs, contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'On a date mutually agreeable' softens the 60-day deadline, and the off-day alternatives are stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-D lets the Publisher determine the long night and restricts nights off, which sits awkwardly with fixing off days by this memorandum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The withholding rule and the 24-hour voucher remedy are stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Times vacation-check letter promises to continue separate vacation checks, which is consistent; 13-B governs the underlying entitlement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Kicked off in variables of five' and 'as heretofore' are trade shorthand that state no ascertainable rule to an outsider.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-H's bundle schedules address loading rather than kick-off, so nothing else in the instrument supplies the missing content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line jurisdictional allocation for a named operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-D.1 recognises airline terminals in the City as delivery points, which is consistent with NMDU jurisdiction over airport pickup.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement merely to 'observe the new conveyor system to determine manpower requirements' creates no determinate obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-C says new mechanical devices shall be operated exclusively by unit employees, and 16-M.3 bars changes in condition without consent, both of which this open-ended observation clause skirts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three precise relief periods, with '20 minutes relief per trailer or part thereof' clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Carlstadt truck-loader clause sets the identical relief periods without the 'or part thereof' language, an unexplained duplication with a small variance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Disputes are sent to a single named individual with no successor mechanism if he is unavailable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-A channels all interpretation disputes to the Joint Standing Committee and Appeals Board, and 16-E prescribes arbitrator selection, so this carve-out to a named person conflicts with the general machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until they are in force' never says when the decisions come into force, and 'the status quo of each existing run until and if it is phased out will be maintained in all details' is a broad and undated freeze.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to interpret 2-E.2 prospectively while 2-E.2(h) gives the Publisher a present right to increase, decrease or discontinue runs, so the two operate on different assumptions.
